name: Live Transcribe Deaf - Relay
oneLine: An iPhone and iPad app that captions face-to-face conversations, with a paid cloud mode in 60+ languages and a free on-device mode that works without internet.

platforms.detail: On the App Store for iPhone and iPad, also listed for Apple silicon Macs and Apple Vision ("Designed for iPad. Not verified for macOS"). Relay's website only offers an iOS download, and a Google Play search finds no Relay app.

deviceRequirements.detail: The App Store lists iOS 18 or later for iPhone, iPadOS 18 for iPad, and macOS 15 with an M1 chip or later for Mac.

roomCaptions.detail: Relay turns speech around you into text as it is spoken. Its website says to place the phone where it can hear.

groupConversations.text: One phone; you can name each speaker
groupConversations.detail: The App Store version notes (May 2026) say you can name each speaker and see which part of the transcript belongs to whom. Relay describes no way to join several phones into one conversation.

languages.detail: Premium transcription covers 60+ languages and Standard (on-device) transcription 18. One line of the App Store description says 90+ languages for Premium; the rest of Relay's pages say 60+. Relay does not publish the list.

offline.text: Yes, Standard mode on the phone, 18 languages
offline.detail: Standard mode uses Apple's speech recognition on the phone, is free and unlimited, and works without internet. Relay says it may be less accurate in hard conditions. It does not switch by itself: when the connection drops, Relay tells you and you switch to Standard.

speakerLabels.detail: Version 1.26 (May 2026) added naming each speaker so you can see which part of the transcript belongs to whom. The current App Store description and website do not describe it further.

translation.detail: Relay's website, FAQ and App Store listing describe captions only; no translation between spoken languages is described. The app's interface can be switched between languages, separately from the language being transcribed.

saveTranscripts.text: Yes, on the phone only, no audio
saveTranscripts.detail: Transcripts are stored only on your device and are never uploaded; Relay says it cannot read them. Audio is not recorded or stored. You can delete transcripts in the app, and uninstalling removes them.

export.detail: A Share button (added in version 1.36, August 2026) sends transcripts to other apps, and the website says you can export transcripts to any app. The file format is not stated.

fileUpload.detail: Relay's pages describe live transcription only, not transcribing audio or video files.

summaries.detail: Apple's App Store story on Relay says it summarises your recent recordings. Relay's own website and App Store description don't describe summaries.

customWords.detail: No way to add your own words or names is described on Relay's website, FAQ or App Store listing.

display.text: Text size, colours, dark mode, high contrast
display.detail: Font size and colours can be changed, with large text for seniors, dark mode, high contrast options and Dynamic Type. Flip mode turns the text so the person across from you can read it.

soundAlerts.detail: Relay's pages describe speech transcription only; no alerts for sounds such as a doorbell or an alarm are described.

phoneCalls.detail: Relay's pages describe face-to-face conversations; captioning phone calls is not described. Despite its name, it is not an FCC relay service (see Free through a government programme).

videoCalls.detail: Captioning Zoom, Teams or Meet calls is not described.

mediaOnDevice.detail: Captioning videos or audio playing on the phone itself is not described.

humanCaptioners.detail: Captions come from speech recognition: a Premium AI engine or Apple's on-device Speech Recognition. No human captioners are described.

signLanguage.detail: No sign language feature is described.

privacy.text: Premium: cloud, audio not stored; Standard: on phone
privacy.detail: Premium streams audio over an encrypted connection for processing and does not store it; Standard mode processes audio on the phone. Transcripts stay on the phone. Relay says it is designed to be HIPAA compatible but advises asking your compliance officer before medical use. Apple's App Privacy section, filled in by the developer, lists identifiers that may be used to track you across other companies' apps and websites.

account.detail: Relay's FAQ and website say no account is required; data stays on the device.

availability.text: App Store in many countries (iOS only)
availability.detail: The App Store lists Relay in the US, UK, Canada, Australia, Germany, France, Türkiye, Japan, Brazil, India and Slovenia (looked up on 28 October 2026). Relay does not publish a country list.

freePlan.detail: Standard transcription is free and unlimited. The higher-accuracy Premium engine needs a subscription or a pack of hours; whether the free tier includes any Premium time is not stated.

price.detail: US App Store, October 2026: Monthly Subscription US$12.99, Yearly Subscription US$89.99, Lite Monthly US$7.99, Lite Yearly US$59.99, plus items named Core (US$22.99) and Pro (US$44.99) with no period shown. Hour packs that never expire: 10 hours US$9.99, 20 hours US$18.99, 100 hours US$89.99. The App Store description says Premium includes 15 hours a month; the FAQ says Relay Pro includes 10 hours a month. Plan hours reset each billing period. No free trial is described.

accessibilityFunding.detail: Relay is sold through App Store subscriptions and hour packs. Its pages don't mention the FCC or phone calls, and its developer is not on the FCC's list of internet-based relay providers (updated June 2026). FCC relay services help people make phone calls and are paid from a state or federal fund.

strengths.text: Standard mode is free, unlimited and runs on the phone, so it captions without internet in 18 languages.
Transcripts stay on the phone only, audio is not stored, and no account is needed.
Flip mode turns the text toward the person across from you, and Quick Phrases show saved messages like "Please speak slower" with one tap.
Plans start at US$7.99 a month (Lite), and hour packs from US$9.99 for 10 hours never expire (US App Store, October 2026).

limits.text: iPhone and iPad only, with iOS 18 or later: there is no Android app.
The higher-accuracy Premium mode needs internet and paid hours; the free Standard mode covers 18 languages.
No live translation, file transcription, custom words or sound alerts are described.
Relay's terms say not to rely on it for critical, life-safety or legal matters.

notes: No Android version: the website offers only 'Download for iOS', the privacy policy speaks of 'our iOS application', and Google Play searches for the app and for the developer found nothing (the developer page URL returned 404). Conflicts: (1) Premium languages: the App Store description says '90+ languages' in its first paragraph and '60+ Languages' further down; the website and FAQ say 60+. (2) Hours included: the App Store description says Premium includes 15 hours a month; the FAQ says 'Relay Pro includes 10 hours (600 minutes)'. The In-App Purchases list has Monthly/Yearly Subscription, Lite Monthly/Yearly, 'Core' (US$22.99) and 'Pro' (US$44.99) with no period or hours shown, so which plan includes how many hours is not clear; 'Yearly Subscription US$89.99' appears twice. (3) Privacy: Apple's App Store story says conversations are 'processed on your iPhone and never uploaded to external servers', but Relay's own privacy policy and FAQ say Premium audio is streamed for processing (not stored); only Standard mode is on the phone. The App Store App Privacy section (developer-declared) lists Identifiers under 'Data Used to Track You' and Third-Party Advertising among purposes, while the privacy policy names only Adapty (subscriptions) and anonymous analytics. (4) The privacy policy's effective date is 'January 6th, 2025' and the terms say 'January 2025', although the App Store lists the app's release as 1 February 2026. (5) The App Store lists 16 interface languages; the description says 10. Summaries are only mentioned in Apple's App Store story, not on Relay's own pages; details unknown. Speaker naming is only in the version notes for 1.26 (May 2026). The FAQ answers are loaded by script; they were read from the site's own JavaScript bundle for /faq. The website's 'Documentation' link on the support page goes back to the homepage. The App Store page's 'More by' section lists other apps by the same seller (an AI note taker, a transcription app and a call-captioning app, 'Realtime Caption Call: CapCall'); Relay's own website does not link them, so they are not mentioned on the comparison page. The name 'Relay' is not related to US relay services: the FCC's list of internet-based relay providers (updated 10 June 2026) does not include the developer, and Relay's pages never mention phone calls or the FCC. Not checked: what the free tier includes beyond Standard mode (any Premium minutes), how speaker naming works live, export formats, and the Quick Phrases/'Type' reply feature in detail (the website mock-up shows Clear, Type, Flip and Text buttons). Not opened: the app itself. All pages read with curl on 2026-10-28.
